metas.name: A-31 Lush Mountains
metas.note:
The eastern part of highway A-31 travels high into the Andes through lush green mountains and valleys.

  • Entirely gen 4 and very sunny.
  • Very high elevation, mountains up in the clouds and views of a vast landscape below.
  • Valleys covered in shrubs, bright green grass, and occasional eucalyptus trees.
  • Scattered rocks beside the road and human-made rock walls.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Alto Biobío National Park
metas.note: Alto Biobío National Park in Araucania can be recognized by all yellow road lines on a high elevation road usually looking down over a vast mountainous landscape. Monkey puzzle trees, short bushes, and bunches of Chilean bamboo cover the ground.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Alto Loa National Reserve
metas.note: Alto Loa can be recognized by its remote and almost completely barren desert landscape featuring reddish gravelly soil and tall snow-capped mountains all around. Salt pans are also common. All coverage is gen 3 and on dirt roads.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Bay of Concepción
metas.note: Locations along the Bay of Concepción can be recognized by the presence of water to the east, north, or west, with the other side of the bay usually visible. Coverage is all gen 4 in developed coastal towns with many small beaches and a lot of boating activity. You'll also see lush coastal vegetation and pine forests.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Bay of Concepción - Ruta 164
metas.note: The stretch of Ruta 164 that follows the coast of the Bay of Concepción can be recognized by the presence of coast to the north and both sides of the Bay visible to the east and west. It's surrounded by a flat landscape of green coastal vegetation.The highrises of Concepción city are often visible to the south.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Beach Road B-440
metas.note: A coastal desert road in gen 3, the B-440 runs along the peninsula north of Antofagasta and is unique in having coast to the south or east. The road is entirely paved and features bright white sandy soil and a long stretch of flatness to the north.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Cerro Castillo National Park
metas.note:
Cerro Castillo National Park in Aysén has sunny gen 3 coverage recognizable by its yellow center lines with white outer lines.

  • Landscape is grassy and lightly forested.
  • Tall beige colored snow-capped mountains and jagged rock formations.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Chaitén Area
metas.note:
Chaitén is a small remote town in southern Los Lagos, recognizable for the forested mountain range towering over the town and the presence of ash and rubble due to a volcanic eruption.

  • A west coast with a gravelly beach.
  • A river and large dead forest to the east of town.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Chiloé Island
metas.note:
Chiloé island is very recognizable due to its lush green rolling landscape, southern vegetation, and unique architecture. Coverage is mostly gen 4 summer, with some areas still gen 3.

  • Rolling green landscape, mild hills and no big mountains. Agricultural and livestock grazing fields surrounded by wooden fences are common.
  • Dense forests of arrayan trees (which have reddish bark), coihue, and eucalyptus.
  • Large hard ferns, iconic Chilean rhubarb, and yellow gorse are common.
  • Unique all-wood architecture with facades of wood shingles. Stilt houses are common.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Coastal Road B-430
metas.note:
The B-430 northwest of Antofagasta is a coastal desert road still in generation 3 featuring:

  • Water to the west, reddish sandy soil, and a towering mountain ridge to the east.
  • Often very hazy/foggy coverage.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Concepción City Proper
metas.note: Concepción is one of the most populous cities in Chile and thus has sprawling neighborhoods and many highrises, modern buildings, and parks in its downtown area. The city also has a very unique blue and yellow street lamp design. Coverage in Concepción is almost entirely gen 4.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Coquimbo City Landmarks
metas.note: The Coquimbo/La Serena urban area is recognizable for being a large coastal city surrounded by a desert-ish landscape. Much of Coquimbo is built on a large hill and features landmarks visible from quite far away: the Third Millennium Cross (a giant metal cross) and the Cultural Mohamed VI (a tall and colorful mosque).
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: East on Ruta 60
metas.note:
East of Rio Branco in Valparaíso, Ruta 60 is recognizable for its gen 4 coverage on a concrete road with all yellow road lines surrounded by dry rocky mountains.

  • Bushes and trees further west near Rio Branco, and low vegetation or bare ground max east.
  • Lots of traffic on the road. Yellow lines on a concrete road is a rare combination, so it's a very good identifier for Ruta 60.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Eastern Santiago Northern Roads
metas.note: The mountain road east of Lo Barnechea has all yellow road lines with a single center line. It goes through dry, rocky mountains with dark brown soil. The elevation increases and vegetation decreases as the road goes east. Bare snow-capped peaks can be seen from the easternmost part.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Eastern Santiago Southern Roads
metas.note: The main mountain road east of Puente Alto is gen 4 and always has large dry mountains on all sides. The northern part of the road has white lines and goes through small towns; the southern part has all yellow lines, less vegetation, and features tall snow-capped peaks visible in the distance.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Embalse el Yeso Gen 3
metas.note: In the mountains east of Santiago, Embalse el Yeso can be recognized by gen 3 coverage traveling along the coast of a bright turquoise reservoir surrounded by extremely tall mountains made of dark rock.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Embalse el Yeso Gen 4
metas.note: The mountain road up to Embalse el Yeso is covered in gen 4 on an unmarked road (or a dirt road). It can be recognized by the deep brown rocky soil beside the road and the giant mountains made of dark rock visible all around. Snow is often visible on top of the mountain ridges.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Futaleufú National Reserve
metas.note: Futaleufú National Reserve is made up of a dense southern forest in a wide mountain-lined valley recognizable for its high number of Patagonian cypress (with thick trunks and round leaf clusters) and the wooden fencing lining every road.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Gen 3 Tamarugo Forests
metas.note:
Tamarugo trees, recognizable for their dark bark and thin, spindly light green leaves, are unique to the central desert plains of Tarapacá.

Smaller clusters of tamarugo trees surrounded by rural houses, signs, and fenced-off land can be found on the A-665 and in the town of La Tirana.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Hualpén Peninsula Gen 3
metas.note: The gen 3 coverage on Hualpén Peninsula can be recognized as a mostly flat coastal area featuring subtropical vegetation and unusually deep red soil. You'll always have water to the south and west, with the highrises of Concepción often visible in the distance.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Hualpén Peninsula Gen 4
metas.note: Gen 4 coverage on the Hualpén Peninsula can be recognized by a combination of coastal vegetation, grassy fields with dark soil, and lush green forests including planted eucalyptus trees. Coast can often be seen to the north, or to the west where the large port of Talcahuano is visible.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: La Serena Beach Road
metas.note: The main road going toward Coquimbo along the coastline of La Serena features rows of fancy resorts, planted palm trees, and a great view of Coquimbo peninsula, which is basically one big hill covered in buildings that juts northward into the ocean. The giant metal Third Millenium Cross is often visible.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: La Serena Historic Center
metas.note: A lot of Spanish neocolonial architecture, very often painted red and white, is a defining feature of La Serena's Historic Center. "La Serena pavement," made of red tiles and with black or grey tiled patterns, is found on most sidewalks (and some roads) in the historic center.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Laguna del Laja National Park
metas.note:
The eastern part of road Q-45 goes into Laguna del Laja National Park, which features a vast landscape and recognizable lush snow-capped mountain ranges.

  • Coverage is all gen 4 on an unpaved road with dark grey or brown dirt.
  • Western part is green and forested. Yellow flowers are common.
  • The middle part features a blue sparkling lake with snow-capped mountains all around.
  • The eastern part by the Argentina border has an open landscape and low greenish vegetation.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Lake Jeinimeni National Reserve
metas.note:
The south part of the X-753 goes into Lake Jeinimeni National Reserve, recognizable for its gen 3 overcast coverage in a fall-colored southern beech forest located right next to snow-capped mountains.

  • Parts of the reserve have snow on the ground.
  • Trees have greyish-brown bark and deep orange or red leaves.
  • Lake Jeinimeni itself has clear blue water and is lined by snow-capped mountains.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Lauca National Park
metas.note:
Generation 3 coverage on a paved road through a barren desert landscape with snow-capped mountain ridges to the north and west is typical of Lauca National Park.

  • The snow-covered Parinacota Volcano is the most distinctive feature of the park.
  • Soil is rocky and covered with small bushes and the green cushion plant "yareta".
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Llanos de Challe National Park
metas.note: Foggy and overcast gen 4 coverage on a paved desert road along the coast is characteristic of Llanos de Challe. The surrounding soil is an orange-brown color, somewhat rocky, and covered in small dark green bushes. There will always be coast west and a large mountain ridge to the east, though the coast can appear quite far away.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Los Flamencos National Reserve
metas.note:
Los Flamencos National Reserve has gen 3 or gen 4 coverage on a paved road, all yellow roadlines, and a barren desert landscape.

  • Gravelly soil that is red or pink. Many hills that look like large sand dunes.
  • Snow-capped mountains can be seen in the west, flatness and random rocks can be seen in the east.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: N-31 Mountain Pass
metas.note:
The eastern part of the N-31 is all gen 4 on an unpaved gravel road going through a wide mountain pass. It features:

  • Very dark and rocky soil. Lots of random rocks beside the road.
  • Dense forest all around, with many bare leafless trees. Small ferns and moss cover the forest floor.
  • Significant snow cover on surrounding mountains.
  • The Ñuble River is often visible close to the road.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: N-55 East of Recinto (Gen 4)
metas.note:
From Recinto to Las Trancas, the N-55 is a gen 4 road with winter coverage in a forested mountain valley.

  • All yellow road lines, wooden fences and stone gutters along the road.
  • Temperate forest in winter, featuring many bare trees. A lot of bright green Chilean bamboo next to the road.
  • Closer to Las Trancas, lots of snow on the ground and on mountain slopes.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: N-55 Gen 3
metas.note: The far eastern part of the N-55 has distinct gen 3 winter coverage on a dirt road going up a mountain slope. The road is surrounded by a trees that are often bare and leafless. A large snow-covered mountain ridge is visible close to the east. Near the top of the mountain, there's snow beside the road.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Nevados Tres Cruces National Park
metas.note:
In Nevado Tres Cruces National Park, Ruta 31 is gen 4 on a wide road with all yellow road lines and dark, grainy asphalt.

  • A semi-open landscape with snow visible on the surrounding mountains.
  • Red-and-yellow snow poles with a rectangular yellow tag on top.
  • Further east, there's dark volcanic soil and a lot more snow on the ground.
  • Max east, Laguna Verde has bright blue water and dark mountains in the background.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Pampa del Tamarugal National Reserve
metas.note: Tamarugo trees, recognizable for their dark bark and thin, spindly light green leaves, are unique to the central desert plains of Tarapacá. Gen 4 coverage through a tamarugo forest usually indicates Pampa del Tamarugal National Reserve where the flat, barren desert suddenly transitions into a large forest.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Patagonia National Park
metas.note: Gen 3 sunny summer coverage on a thin dirt road in a green mountain valley characterizes Patagonia National Park in Aysén. It is a lush rolling grassland with large hills south and a massive, snow-capped mountain range to the north. A particular green cushion plant ("Patagonian Azorella") is endemic to the area.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Puyehue Max East
metas.note: The far eastern part of Puyehue National Park features all yellow road lines on a poor-quality road with tar between the center lines. Recognizable white-and-yellow snow poles line the road. The surrounding landscape is a high-altitude coihue forest with light sandy soil.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Puyehue National Park
metas.note: In gen 4, all yellow road lines on a poor quality road (with cracks, potholes, etc.), surrounded by a southern beech forest with dense undergrowth is characteristic of Puyehue National Park. The undergrowth features a lot of ferns, bamboo, and Chilean rhubarb. In the eastern part of the park, all of the trees look dead and are completely bare of leaves.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Q-45 East of Antuco
metas.note:
East of Antuco, the Q-45 runs through a very recognizable green mountain valley. It features:

  • Gen 4 coverage on a nicely-paved road with all yellow road lines. Some sections are overcast while others are bright and sunny.
  • Tall mountain ridges on both sides, covered in dense green forest.
  • Many mountains go up through the clouds, and some mountains are snow-capped.
  • In sunny coverage, blooming yellow flowers are everywhere.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Road R-95-S
metas.note:
Road R-95-S is covered in gen 4 on a light gravel road running through a vast and open landscape surrounded by mountains.

  • Small shrubs and round tufts of grass cover the hills.
  • Sparse forests of pines and southern beech trees cover the landscape.
  • A large number of Monkey puzzle trees can also be seen.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Road W-887
metas.note:
The W-887 in max south Los Lagos is short but very memorable. It can be recognized by overcast or rainy coverage on a dark dirt road surrounded by Patagonian trees.

  • It often has white sand/ash on or alongside the road.
  • Lots of Chilean rhubarb and massive hard ferns.
  • Sometimes there are visible water droplets on the camera.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Road X-753
metas.note:
The X-753 goes south of Chile Chico and is recognizable by entirely overcast gen 3 fall coverage, a dark brown dirt road, and a very dry mountainous landscape.

  • Reddish soil covered in small yellow or green bushes. Basically no trees or human activity at all.
  • A distinctive snow-covered mountain range to the west.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Ruta 11 in the Mountains
metas.note: Up in the mountains, Ruta 11 features gen 4 on a newly-paved road with a reddish tinge, surrounded by a high altitude landscape composed of completely bare pinkish mountains and bright white rocks. Double guardrails, concrete barriers (sometimes painted yellow), and active construction sites are all common.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Ruta 11 in the Mountains (with vegetation)
metas.note: Up in the mountains and around Zapahuira, Ruta 11 features all gen 4 coverage on a wide, newly-paved road with a high altitude mountainous landscape that is covered in small green or grey bushes. The surrounding mountains are typically rounded on top, with snow-capped peaks sometimes distantly visible to the north.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Ruta 11 River Valley
metas.note:
Ruta 11 is entirely sunny gen 4 coverage. The river valley section is recognizable for:

  • Sloping, sandy mountains on either side of the valley.
  • Large agricultural fields and planted Mexican fan palms.
  • A railroad runs along the entire valley and is often visible north or south of the road.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Ruta 115
metas.note:
In eastern Maule, Ruta 115 travels deep into the Andes through a beautiful mountain valley. Coverage is all early spring gen 4 and has yellow road lines (either yellow center or all yellow).

  • The valley is extremely wide and has temperate forest vegetation. Many trees are bare due to the season.
  • Immense rocky mountains covered in trees, grass, and shrubs are always visible. Many have snow-covered peaks.
  • The easternmost stretch goes to high altitude and has scarce vegetation and a lot of snow everywhere.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Ruta 15 Eastern Part
metas.note:
Far east on Ruta 15 is gen 4 on a paved road surrounded by a semi-flat landscape covered in Peruvian feathergrass and small shrubs, with towering mountains in the distance.

  • Soil is light, reddish, and very sandy.
  • Andean plateau vegetation like feathergrass, tola, and yareta are common.
  • Mountain ranges are often snow-capped and they appear closer further east.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Ruta 15 in the Andean Plateau
metas.note:
The eastern part of Ruta 15 is a gen 4 paved road that goes through the high altitude Andean Plateau. It has:

  • Light brown or reddish soil that is covered in feathergrass, the spindly tola shrub, and occasionally the green blob-shaped yareta. rolling hills
  • Round rolling hills with occasional exposed cliff faces.
  • One section around Chapire has all yellow road lines.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Ruta 15 Max East Grassland
metas.note:
Right near the Bolivian border, Ruta 15 goes through a flat green grassland surrounded by towering, often snow-capped volcanoes.

  • Coverage is all gen 4. Ruta 15 itself is paved, side roads are unpaved.
  • Buildings often use Bolivian-style red brick architecture.
  • Small waterways and grazing llamas are also common.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Ruta 181
metas.note:
Ruta 181 in Araucania can be recognized by sunny gen 4 coverage on a road with all yellow roadlines. It particularly features:

  • A vast open landscape surrounded by large rocky mountains.
  • Lush green forests on mountainsides.
  • Open grassy fields between hills, often enclosed by wooden fences.
  • An abundance of planted poplar and mediterranean cypress trees.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Ruta 225 in Los Lagos
metas.note:
Ruta 225 in Los Lagos runs between Puerto Varas and Petrohue and is recognizable for its unique infrastructure, beautiful views, and native coihue forests. It features:

  • Completely gen 4 coverage, unique wooden guardrails, and a paved two-way bike lane next to the road.
  • Dark soil and a lot of ferns growing from the ground.
  • Dense forest of coihue, particularly further east.
  • Views of the snow-capped Osorno and Calbuco volcanoes.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Ruta 240 and Río Simpson
metas.note:
Ruta 240 to Puerto Aysén is recognizable for being summer coverage on a concrete road with a single yellow center line.

  • It goes through a wide valley between huge mountains that have exposed cliff faces.
  • Area is very forested with southern beech trees and planted poplars.
  • Purple flowers (large-leaved lupines) and Chilean rhubarb along the road.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Ruta 31, West of Nevado Tres Cruces
metas.note:
Sunny gen 4 coverage on an unmarked desert road with red or dark brown soil strongly indicates Ruta 31. Notably, the section west of Nevado Tres Cruces National Park features:

  • Usually very red soil and a complete lack of vegetation, especially on unpaved sections. Paved sections have no road lines.
  • Large, sloped mountains with rounded peaks. Visible snow on some mountains.
  • Large Y-shaped metal pylons running alongside the road.
  • Part of the road climbs to high altitude and has significant snow on the ground as well as yellow-and-white snow poles.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Ruta 41 Gen 4
metas.note:
In Coquimbo, where Ruta 41 enters the Andes, it has distinct gen 4 coverage on a paved road that features steep snow-capped mountains visible to the east.

  • Large rocky mountains on all sides; lots of snow cover atop the tallest mountains.
  • All yellow road lines start around Miraflores and continue further east.
  • Planted trees and fenced-off vineyards closer to Vicuña. Many vineyards go right up to the base of mountains.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Ruta 9
metas.note:
Ruta 9 in Magallanes is a unique concrete road with yellow center and outside lines surrounded by a Patagonian landscape.

  • It's gen 3 and usually has overcast coverage.
  • Flat or slight rolling hills covered in grassy fields and sparse trees.
  • Part of it runs along an eastern coast.
  • Close to Cerro Castillo there are much more significant hills.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Ruta 9 Divided Section
metas.note:
Ruta 9 in Magallanes is a concrete road with yellow road lines, surrounded by a Patagonian landscape of dark soil and grassy hills.

  • Starting at the Punta Arenas airport and going south through Punta Arenas, Ruta 9 is a divided highway.
  • Punta Arenas is a large and recognizable urban area and is usually visible.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Ruta 9 Max South
metas.note:
Ruta 9 in Magallanes is iconic and very distinct. It's unique for being a concrete road with yellow center and outside lines, combined with a deep south Patagonian environment of dark soil and rolling grassy hills.

  • Max south, starting around Bahía Carrera, it turns into an unpaved grey dirt road and enters a southern beech forest.
  • Check the distance and angle of the eastern coast to make precise guesses.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Rutas 201/203
metas.note:
Rutas 201 and 203 in Los Ríos have gen 4 coverage, all yellow road lines, a forested mountainous landscape, and views of large blue lakes.

  • Forests have a dense understory of hard ferns, moss, and Chilean bamboo.
  • Early spring coverage, so many trees have sparse light green leaves.
  • Many views of Lake Calafquén or Lake Panguipulli, with pure blue water and large snow-capped mountains in the background.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Rutas 21 and 25 Sunset Coverage
metas.note: The stretch of highway on Ruta 25 to Calama and on Ruta 21 from Calama to San Francisco de Chiu Chiu has memorable gen 4 sunset coverage, recognizable by how dark it is and its generally east-west road angle.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: San Pedro de Atacama
metas.note:
The town of San Pedro de Atacama is a sizeable settlement (by Atacama desert standards) recognizable for the abundance of iconic adobe (mudbrick) buildings.

  • The adobe used is a reddish/deep brown color but is often painted white and red.
  • Adobe walls frequently have unique triangular ornamentations.
  • The large Licanabur volcano is often visible to the north/east.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Santa Catalina Tamarugo Forest
metas.note:
Tamarugo trees, recognizable by their dark bark and thin/spindly green or yellow leaves, are unique to the central plains of Tarapacá. A stretch of Ruta 5 near Santa Catalina passes through a Tamarugo forest.

  • It's all sunny gen 4 and looks similar to Pampa del Tamarugal National Reserve.
  • A line of scissor-topped poles run to the east along this stretch of road.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: The "Devil's Throat"
metas.note:
Just north of San Pedro de Atacama, there's scenic gen 4 coverage in a shallow canyon so-called the "Devil's Throat". It has:

  • Reddish, rocky canyon walls displaying sediment layers.
  • Unique sharp and wavy rock formations.
  • Greyish-green shrubs and tufts of grass.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: V-69 Near Cochamó
metas.note:
The V-69 in southeastern Los Lagos runs along a beautiful fjord with water west and views of huge snow-capped mountains across the water.

  • All coverage is gen 4 on a road that's paved north of Cochamó and unpaved south of it.
  • Recognizable snowy mountains with visible clouds hovering below the mountain peaks.
  • The town of Cochamó is recognizable as a cluster of houses on the coast of the fjord and surrounded by massive snowy mountains.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Villa O'Higgins
metas.note:
Villa O'Higgins, the southernmost town in Aysén, is recognizable by gen 3 sunset coverage in a small, organized town surrounded by massive snow-capped mountains.

  • Coverage was taken late fall, so the southern beech forests around the town display deep orange leaves.
  • Soil is dark brown or grey.
  • Houses are made entirely of wood with sheet metal roofs.
  • Streets are usually made of small alternating stone tiles and have stone curbs on either side.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Villarrica National Park
metas.note:
Ruta 199 through Villarrica National Park can be recognized by sunny gen 4 coverage on a wide paved road, all yellow road lines, and a landscape of towering mountains and dense forests.

  • Mountains often feature exposed cliff faces.
  • Often has concrete drainage ditches on both sides of the road.
  • In the southeastern part, you'll often see Monkey puzzle trees and the enormous Lanín volcano.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: Viña del Mar Coastline
metas.note:
Viña del Mar/Valparaíso is Chile's largest coastal city, most recognizable by its fancy highrises, hilly neighborhoods, and beautiful coastline. The road going along its coast is covered in gen 4 and features:

  • Water close to the west and tall city highrises close to the east.
  • An avenue of fancy white hotels and resorts along the coast; many planted palm trees along the road.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: X-25 Max East Sunset Coverage
metas.note:
The max east part of X-25 in Aysén features dark sunset coverage, fall colors, a mostly flat barren landscape, and low-lying mountains in the background.

  • Coverage is on a dark grey dirt road.
  • Surrounded by small bushes and round tufts of grass; landscape almost completely devoid of trees.
metas.footer: Check out A Learnable Chile - Guide for more detailed explanations.

metas.name: X-25 Sunset Coverage
metas.note:
East of Seccion Tapera in Aysén, the X-25 is very recognizable for its late sunset coverage, striking fall colors, and semi-dry landscape with sparse trees and low bushes.

  • Sunset coverage gets later the further east you go.
  • Coverage is on a dark grey dirt road.
  • Hills around the road; a large snow-capped mountain ridge off to the north.

metas.name: Y-150 and Y-156 in Torres del Paine
metas.note:
Going through Torres del Paine National Park in Magallanes, the Y-150 is recognizable for its rocky mountainous landscape, dark soil, and dry Patagonian vegetation.

  • A dark (almost black) northwesterly snow-capped mountain ridge close to the road.
  • "Iceland-esque" grassy hills with areas of dark exposed rock.
  • Runs along multiple bodies of water.
